audit_notes: Model: 1D shear of the bead-filled soft foundation with the silicone skin in series (skin compliance added in the metric transform). Bead stiffening of the foundation by rigid spheres (Guth-Gold): volume fraction phi_v = area fraction * (2/3) d / t_f = 0.5*0.667e-3/1.5e-3 = 0.222, G_eff = G(1 + 2.5 phi + 14.1 phi^2) = 2.25 G = 4.5e5 Pa. This is a correction the proposal's estimate missed (it used the unfilled modulus): compliance C = t_f/G_eff + t_s/G_s = 3.33e-9 + 3.0e-10 = 3.6e-9 m/Pa (not 7.8e-9), sigma_c = sqrt(2*0.05/3.6e-9) = 5.2 kPa. Baseline: standard silicone foul-release (0.3 mm, G 0.33 MPa, no beads, no separate skin): C = 9.1e-10 m/Pa, sigma_c = 10.5 kPa -> expected ~50% lower release stress (vs -15% for the tiled parent), because the fouler now sees silicone (w_a 0.05) instead of epoxy tiles. Further caveats: local compliance above a bead crest is only t_s/G_s + (t_f - d)/G_f ~ 1.8e-9 m/Pa - barnacles centred on crests see ~40% higher release stress; Guth-Gold is approximate for phi > 0.2. Drag: overcoated bead waviness 5-10 um amplitude over ~1-2 mm, k+ ~ 1 and slopes < 1% -> hydraulically smooth; wall shear change vs baseline 0 +/- 0.5% (not modelled). Durability: beads limit indentation/gouge depth under blunt loads and carry fender contact; skin still abraded by brushes over crests. Applicability: broadcast aggregate into wet coating is a standard deck-coating technique, feasible in dry dock. Dimensionless: phi_v = 0.22, G_eff/G = 2.25, skin compliance share 8%, bead crest compliance ratio 0.5.
